question: Which enzyme do corticosteroids block to stop the body's inflammatory process?
explanation: Spot on! Steroids block phospholipase A2 right at the beginning of the inflammation pathway, which stops inflammatory chemicals from ever forming. You've got this! [learn more](GNS223_U5_T3#GNS223_U5_T3_h1)

question: Why are corticosteroids much stronger at reducing inflammation than regular pain relievers?

options.A: They completely eliminate white blood cells.
options.B: They only target localized pain receptors in joints.
options.C: They act higher up the inflammatory chain by stopping chemical production at the source.
options.D: They work instantly within seconds to repair tissue.

explanation: Brilliant! Because they block the chain reaction right at the source (phospholipase A2), steroids have a powerful, whole-body anti-inflammatory effect. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T3#GNS223_U5_T3_h1)

question: Which of these medications is classified as a long-acting corticosteroid?
explanation: Correct! Dexamethasone is a long-acting steroid that stays active in the body for 36 to 72 hours. Keep up the great revision! [learn more](GNS223_U5_T3#GNS223_U5_T3_h2)

question: What is the main difference between short-acting and long-acting corticosteroids?

options.A: How long they remain active in the body and their strength.
options.B: Whether they require a doctor's prescription.
options.C: If they cause weight gain during long-term therapy.
options.D: Whether they are swallowed or injected into a muscle.

explanation: You got it! Different steroid types stay in the system for different lengths of time and have varying strengths for reducing swelling. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T3#GNS223_U5_T3_h2)

question: Which route of administration is best for treating a sudden, life-threatening allergic reaction?
explanation: Spot on! The intravenous (IV) route pushes the medication straight into the bloodstream for instant action during emergencies. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T3#GNS223_U5_T3_h3)

question: A patient with severe arthritis in one knee gets a direct steroid injection into the joint. What is the main benefit?

options.A: It lets the drug bypass the liver to enter the brain instantly.
options.B: It gives high drug concentration at the problem site while sparing the rest of the body.
options.C: It completely cures the underlying autoimmune disease.
options.D: It guarantees no side effects like high blood pressure.

explanation: Correct! Giving the injection right into the knee treats the local pain while keeping whole-body side effects as low as possible. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T3#GNS223_U5_T3_h3)

question: What is a major reason doctors prescribe corticosteroids for lung conditions?

options.A: To thin thick mucus so coughing is easier
options.B: To reduce airway swelling during severe asthma attacks
options.C: To kill bacterial germs inside the lungs
options.D: To lower high blood pressure in lung vessels

explanation: Well done! Steroids are powerful anti-inflammatory drugs that quickly open up swollen airways when an asthma attack strikes. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T3#GNS223_U5_T3_h4)

question: How do corticosteroids help patients with autoimmune diseases like lupus?

options.A: By calming an overactive immune system that is attacking healthy tissues
options.B: By destroying abnormal white blood cells in bone marrow
options.C: By rebuilding damaged joint cartilage and bone
options.D: By replacing lost vitamins in the blood

explanation: Spot on! In autoimmune conditions, the body attacks itself. Steroids act like a peacekeeper, calming down that overactive immune response. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T3#GNS223_U5_T3_h4)

question: Which of the following is a common long-term side effect of taking corticosteroids?

options.C: Rapid muscle building and weight loss

explanation: Correct! Long-term steroid use messes with calcium and bone building, which can lead to fragile bones over time. Good clinical knowledge! [learn more](GNS223_U5_T3#GNS223_U5_T3_h5)

question: A patient taking high-dose prednisone for six months reports feeling very hungry all the time and notices weight gain around the face and neck. What causes this?

options.A: Fluid is building up inside the brain tissue.
options.B: Steroids alter how the body stores fat and stimulates appetite.
options.C: The medication is destroying the thyroid gland completely.
options.D: The patient is secretly eating too much junk food at night.

explanation: Corticosteroids alter carbohydrate and fat metabolism, frequently causing increased appetite and fat redistribution. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T3#GNS223_U5_T3_h5)

question: When should a nurse question a doctor's order to start systemic corticosteroid therapy?

options.A: When the patient has an active, untreated fungal infection
options.B: When the patient has stable, controlled blood pressure
options.C: When the patient had childhood asthma
options.D: When the patient has mild seasonal allergies

explanation: Spot on! Because steroids suppress the immune system, giving them during an active infection lets the infection run wild. Always check for infections first! [learn more](GNS223_U5_T3#GNS223_U5_T3_h6)

question: Why is taking corticosteroids together with NSAIDs (like ibuprofen) a big risk?

options.A: It causes blood pressure to drop dangerously low.
options.B: It cancels out the steroid so it doesn't work.
options.C: It greatly increases the chance of stomach ulcers and bleeding.
options.D: It stops the liver from filtering other drugs.

explanation: Brilliant! Both drugs irritate the stomach lining. Combining them multiplies the risk of painful ulcers and internal bleeding. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T3#GNS223_U5_T3_h6)

question: Which lab value or vital sign must be checked regularly for patients on long-term corticosteroids?
explanation: Correct! Steroids trigger the liver to release stored sugar, which often leads to high blood sugar levels that need close monitoring. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T3#GNS223_U5_T3_h7)

question: Why is daily weight tracking so important for a patient taking oral prednisone?

options.A: It helps catch fluid retention and rapid water weight gain early.
options.B: It calculates the exact dose needed for the next day.
options.C: It proves the patient is absorbing pills through the stomach.
options.D: It ensures the patient is following a workout routine.

explanation: Spot on! Steroids cause the body to hold onto salt and water, making daily weigh-ins a great way to spot fluid overload early. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T3#GNS223_U5_T3_h7)

question: What life-threatening emergency can happen if a patient stops taking long-term steroids all of a sudden?
explanation: You nailed it! Stopping steroids abruptly when the adrenal glands are inactive throws the body into a dangerous crash called an addisonian crisis. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T3#GNS223_U5_T3_h8)

question: Why must long-term steroid therapy be gradually tapered off instead of stopped overnight?

options.A: It gives the adrenal glands time to wake up and make natural hormones again.
options.B: It gives the liver time to clear leftover chemicals.
options.C: It keeps the original disease from coming back instantly.
options.D: It stops the patient from feeling sudden weight loss and fatigue.

explanation: Brilliant! Long-term steroids put the body's natural hormone factories (adrenals) to sleep. Tapering slowly wakes them back up safely. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T3#GNS223_U5_T3_h8)

question: What advice should a nurse give a patient taking oral prednisone to protect their stomach?

options.A: Take the medication on an empty stomach.
options.B: Crush the pills and dissolve them in juice.
options.C: Take the medication right before going to bed.
options.D: Take the medication with food or milk.

explanation: Correct! Steroids can be harsh on the gut lining, so taking them with food, milk, or a meal helps prevent stomach upset. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T3#GNS223_U5_T3_h9)

question: A patient on long-term steroid therapy asks why they need a medical alert bracelet. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: It proves to your insurance that you take your pills.
options.B: It warns people around you that you might gain weight.
options.C: It lets emergency staff know your adrenal glands are asleep if you have an accident.
options.D: It stops doctors from giving you new prescriptions.

explanation: Spot on! In an emergency, medical staff need to know your adrenal system is suppressed so they can provide extra steroid support your body can't make on its own. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T3#GNS223_U5_T3_h9)
